questions.enonce_markdown:
9. Why did the USA enter the Second World War in 1941? What contribution did it make to the defeat of the Axis powers? What were the consequences of this defeat?

**(7/7/6marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Second World War began in Europe in September 1939. The United States, which had kept out of the war, entered it on **7-8 December 1941**. The Axis powers were Germany, Italy and Japan.

**1. Why the USA entered the war in 1941 (7 marks).**
- **The attack on Pearl Harbor.** On **7 December 1941** Japan launched a surprise air attack on the American naval base of **Pearl Harbor** in Hawaii, sinking or damaging many ships and killing about two thousand four hundred Americans. The next day, **8 December**, the US Congress declared war on Japan. On **11 December** Germany and Italy, allies of Japan, declared war on the United States, which then entered the war against all three Axis powers.
- **Japan's expansion.** Japan had invaded China (1937) and then French Indochina (1940-1941), threatening American interests in the Pacific. The USA reacted by freezing Japanese assets and cutting off oil and steel (summer 1941); Japan, which depended on oil imports, saw war as the way to secure resources in South-East Asia, and attacked the American fleet first.
- **Growing support for the Allies.** Before Pearl Harbor the USA, though neutral, was already helping Britain (destroyers-for-bases 1940; **Lend-Lease Act, March 1941**), and the Atlantic Charter (August 1941) showed that Roosevelt and Churchill shared war aims; American public opinion turned against Germany and Japan.
- **The threat of Nazi Germany and Fascism** to democracy and to American trade.

**2. The contribution of the USA to the defeat of the Axis (7 marks).**
- **Industrial production.** The USA became the "arsenal of democracy": its factories produced vast numbers of aircraft, tanks, ships, trucks and weapons, which were also supplied to Britain, the Soviet Union and China by Lend-Lease.
- **In the Pacific.** The American navy stopped Japan at the battles of the **Coral Sea (May 1942)** and **Midway (June 1942)**, and the "island-hopping" campaign (Guadalcanal and other islands) brought American forces close to Japan.
- **In Africa and Europe.** American troops landed in North Africa (**Operation Torch, November 1942**), took part in the invasion of Sicily and Italy (1943) and, under General **Eisenhower**, in the **D-Day landings in Normandy (6 June 1944)**, which opened the Western Front and led to the liberation of France; Germany surrendered in **May 1945**.
- **Air power.** Allied (British and American) bombing destroyed German and Japanese industry and cities.
- **The atomic bomb.** The USA developed the first atomic bombs (the Manhattan Project) and dropped them on **Hiroshima (6 August 1945)** and **Nagasaki (9 August 1945)**; Japan surrendered in August and signed the surrender on **2 September 1945**.

**3. Consequences of the defeat of the Axis powers (6 marks).**
- **Occupation and trial of the defeated powers.** Germany was divided into four occupation zones (and later into East and West Germany); Japan was occupied by the USA under General MacArthur and received a new democratic constitution. The leaders were tried at **Nuremberg** (1945-1946) and in **Tokyo** (1946-1948).
- **End of Fascism and Nazism** in Germany, Italy and Japan.
- **Creation of the United Nations (1945)** to maintain peace.
- **The USA and the USSR became the two superpowers**, and their rivalry led to the **Cold War**; Western Europe, ruined by the war, received American aid (the Marshall Plan).
- **Decline of the European colonial empires.** Britain and France were weakened and African and Asian nationalists demanded independence, which led to decolonisation.
- **Human and material losses.** Millions of soldiers and civilians died, including the Jews murdered in the Holocaust, and many cities were destroyed.
